hints: Apply \(\tan(A\pm B)=(\tan A\pm\tan B)/(1\mp\tan A\tan B)\) to both sides.
Set \(t=\tan\theta\), use \(\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3\), clear denominators, and simplify to a quadratic in t.
Solve the quadratic, then for each value of \(\tan\theta\) find all angles in \(0^\circ\le\theta\le180^\circ\).
walkthrough:
Recall the compound angle formulas for the tangent function:
$$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A\tan B} \quad \text{and} \quad \tan(A - B) = \dfrac{\tan A - \tan B}{1 + \tan A\tan B}$$

Substitute the exact special angle value $\tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}$ into both compound angle expansions:
$$\tan(\theta + 60^\circ) = \dfrac{\tan\theta + \sqrt{3}}{1 - \sqrt{3}\tan\theta}$$
$$\tan(60^\circ - \theta) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - \tan\theta}{1 + \sqrt{3}\tan\theta}$$

Let $t = \tan\theta$ to simplify algebraic working:
$$\dfrac{t + \sqrt{3}}{1 - \sqrt{3}t} = 2 + \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - t}{1 + \sqrt{3}t}$$

Move the tangent terms to the left-hand side:
$$\dfrac{t + \sqrt{3}}{1 - \sqrt{3}t} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - t}{1 + \sqrt{3}t} = 2$$

Combine the two fractions on the left-hand side over a common denominator $(1 - \sqrt{3}t)(1 + \sqrt{3}t)$:
$$\dfrac{(t + \sqrt{3})(1 + \sqrt{3}t) - (\sqrt{3} - t)(1 - \sqrt{3}t)}{(1 - \sqrt{3}t)(1 + \sqrt{3}t)} = 2$$

Expand the numerator:
$$(t + \sqrt{3})(1 + \sqrt{3}t) = t + \sqrt{3}t^2 + \sqrt{3} + 3t = \sqrt{3} + 4t + \sqrt{3}t^2$$
$$(\sqrt{3} - t)(1 - \sqrt{3}t) = \sqrt{3} - 3t - t + \sqrt{3}t^2 = \sqrt{3} - 4t + \sqrt{3}t^2$$
Subtracting the two expressions gives:
$$(\sqrt{3} + 4t + \sqrt{3}t^2) - (\sqrt{3} - 4t + \sqrt{3}t^2) = 4t - (-4t) = 8t$$

Expand the denominator using the difference of two squares $(1 - u)(1 + u) = 1 - u^2$:
$$(1 - \sqrt{3}t)(1 + \sqrt{3}t) = 1^2 - (\sqrt{3}t)^2 = 1 - 3t^2$$

Rearrange into standard quadratic form $at^2 + bt + c = 0$:
$$6t^2 + 8t - 2 = 0$$

Divide the entire equation by $2$ to obtain the required quadratic equation in $\tan\theta$:
$$3\tan^2\theta + 4\tan\theta - 1 = 0$$

Solve this quadratic equation for $\tan\theta$ using the quadratic formula $t = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ with $a = 3$, $b = 4$, $c = -1$:
$$\tan\theta = \dfrac{-4 \pm \sqrt{4^2 - 4(3)(-1)}}{2(3)} = \dfrac{-4 \pm \sqrt{16 + 12}}{6} = \dfrac{-4 \pm \sqrt{28}}{6} = \dfrac{-4 \pm 2\sqrt{7}}{6} = \dfrac{-2 \pm \sqrt{7}}{3}$$

Find the corresponding angle in the interval $0^\circ \le \theta \le 180^\circ$:
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.215250) \approx 12.149^\circ \approx 12.1^\circ$$

Find the corresponding angle in the interval $0^\circ \le \theta \le 180^\circ$:
$$\theta = 180^\circ + \tan^{-1}(-1.548584) = 180^\circ - 57.149^\circ = 122.851^\circ \approx 122.9^\circ$$

State the final solution set within $0^\circ \le \theta \le 180^\circ$:
$$\theta = 12.1^\circ \quad \text{or} \quad 122.9^\circ$$
